name: route-card
title: Route Card
description: A trip card: a line fills behind a plane between two big codes, above a slowly turning globe of dots.

perf.budget: The globe redraws a few hundred dots on the UI thread at 30 fps while on screen, so it animates at rest. The plane only moves when progress changes.

measurements.notes: Animating at rest: the globe turns at 30 fps. An old mid-range phone; the numbers include scrolling the demo page.

a11y.reducedMotion: The globe holds still and the plane jumps to its place.
a11y.screenReader: One progress bar reading the route and times ("IST, ISTANBUL, to NRT, TOKYO. BOARDS: 09:40AM, LANDS: 03:25PM. ON SCHEDULE. KN204.") with "58% of the way".

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { RouteCard } from '@/components/kinetik/route-card';

<RouteCard
  from={{ code: 'IST', city: 'ISTANBUL', time: '09:40AM' }}
  to={{ code: 'NRT', city: 'TOKYO', time: '03:25PM' }}
  status="ON SCHEDULE"
  tag="KN204"
  progress={elapsed / duration}
/>;
```

## When to use

- The main card for a trip under way: a flight, a long train, a sea crossing.
- A hero widget where the globe has room to breathe, next to smaller cards such as Arrival Card and Cruise Dial.

## When not to use

- Lists of trips: every card runs its own turning globe. Use Flight Track instead.
- Trips with stops: one line cannot show them.

## Notes

- `progress` is yours to compute. Each change glides the plane along the line.
- Pass your logo as `mark`, or `null` for none.
- The globe's land is a rough, stylised shape, not a map. Do not use it to show real positions.
- The plane is the Tabler Icons plane (MIT licence, via iconstack.io).

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add route-card`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
